body:
Hey Dimitris

I'm not sure there is actually an issue here. 

On startup the SMF tries to PFCP associate with the UPF, as you have configured the UPF peer in `smf.yaml`. Was the UPF running at `10:47:57`? 

The UPF log file shows it was launched at `10:49:55`, and within 2 seconds the SMF has connected to it, and they enter the PFCP associated state.

Kenny

Hi @kbarlee ,

The UPF was running at that time. I just restarted the service to have a clearer view of the log file.

They indeed entered the PFCP associate state, but the SMF disengaged and tried to reconnect multiple times, even though UPF was still in the associate state.

Dimitris

@dimitrisbro 

I cannot re-produce your situation. If you can re-produce it, please describe the order of running exactly.

Thanks a lot!
Sukchan

I can't understand why it works like this at all, but here's what I've analyzed:

If you look at the pcap of smf/upf, there is PFCP Association Request/Response in packets 1 and 2. But, there is a difference of 10 seconds.

Here is upf.log file
```
04/22 07:57:27.663: [pfcp] DEBUG: Association Setup Response (../lib/pfcp/build.c:190)
04/22 07:57:37.675: [pfcp] DEBUG: [1] REMOTE UPD TX-6  peer [192.168.3.4]:8805 (../lib/pfcp/xact.c:193)
```

There should be no delay in this place, but there is an interval of 10 seconds. And, smf.log doesn't have anything about 04/22 07:57:37.675.

I don't know why this works in your environment. Therefore, it seems to be possible to analyze further by adding a debug message.

Thanks a lot!

Hello @acetcom, i did some debugging and the problem seems to be generated at line 64 of `socketaddr.c` by `getnameinfo()` call. Particullary, when the code tries to execute the translation of socket address the DNS is unreachable and generates a timeout (after 10 second). This depends on my infrastructure and it happens for different reasons. The problem could be bypassed adding a rule in /etc/hosts for example. Anyway, i don't know why with versione 2.0.21 it works.

@DendoD96 

Wow! You're a hero.

Now I can understand why it takes 10 seconds between Request and Response. Basically, I think that the current code is not good. If DNS cannot be reached, it may take 10 seconds event if the users uses the IP address.

So I'll change the current code to make it more intuitive to understand.

For your reference, I believe that there is no difference between v2.0.21 and v2.0.22 for this PFCP area.. If I can find something else, I'll let you know.

Thank you so much!
Sukchan
@acetcom Yes, this is the point: the request is made even if you use IP addresses. It was fun to contribute a little to this wonderful project!

@DendoD96 

I've updated it to the main branch. Now Open5GS does not use getnameinfo() which cause DNS query delay. Please let me know if you have any other problems.

Thank you so much!
Sukchan
